sections.h2: Sales routes for a Decatur homeowner
sections.html:
A Decatur owner has three ways out: list with an agent, sell privately, or deal with a cash buyer who takes the house with its flaws. The state of the roof, furnace and foundation, plus how soon you need the money, usually points to one of them.

  • Listing with an agent pays off for a clean, well-kept house and an owner who can wait out showings, an appraisal and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Selling privately saves the commission, though you handle the price, the paperwork and every negotiation.
  • Cash sales are common for estates, rented houses, homes behind on payments, and properties needing work that a lender would refuse to finance.

Values in Decatur sit far below those in the Chicago suburbs, so one large repair bill can swallow much of a seller's margin. An as-is sale can then net close to what a polished listing would.

sections.h2: Decatur home prices and the market
sections.html:
Decatur is the Macon County seat, in the middle of Illinois. Population has slipped from 71,399 to 67,884, a drop of 4.9 percent, so price from recent local sales and not from older figures. Prices are modest, and nearly four in ten homes are rented.

At roughly $100,000, a single new roof or furnace can equal a noticeable slice of a house's worth. That arithmetic explains why many owners here lean toward selling as-is. Buyers also check which school district a parcel falls in, since most addresses are in Decatur Public Schools District 61 and a few spill into neighboring districts.

sections.h2: Macon County offices for a Decatur sale
sections.html:
Three offices share the Macon County Office Building at 141 South Main Street. Each opens at 8:30 in the morning and closes at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, except legal holidays.

  • Recorder, Room 201, (217) 424-1359. Files deeds and mortgages, maintains a tract index more than 150 years old, and takes electronic filings through vendors such as CSC and Simplifile.
  • Treasurer, Room 302, (217) 424-1426. Sends the annual tax bill and provides duplicates.
  • Supervisor of Assessments, Room 401, (217) 424-1364. Publishes assessments, applies exemptions and serves as clerk to the Board of Review.

The state transfer tax comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10, which sets 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. Ask the Recorder's counter whether Macon County adds a stamp of its own.

sections.h2: Property tax billing and unpaid taxes
sections.html:
Macon County runs a year behind: the bill mailed in May covers the previous tax year. The first installment comes due 30 days after the mailing date, and the second falls on September 1, shifting to the next working day when that date is a weekend or Labor Day.

At a sale, read the settlement statement and ask the title company who owes the bill. Paying late is costly: 1.5 percent attaches for every month or part of a month. Once the second installment passes, a certified delinquency notice goes out with $10 added, and the unpaid amount is auctioned to tax buyers who open at 9 percent and bid downward. A house lived in by its owner generally gets 30 to 36 months to redeem.

A duplicate bill costs $1.00 with proof of ownership. New owners should send the Treasurer a change-of-address form by March 15.

Disputing a value has a short fuse: 30 days from the day your township's figures run in the local paper. Complaints are filed with the Board of Review, and the assessor's staff recommend attaching comparable sales, an appraisal or a settlement statement.

If you owe taxes at closing, the title company normally deducts the balance from your proceeds and pays the Treasurer directly, so ask for a written payoff figure a few days beforehand. Bring the parcel number to the Treasurer's office (Room 302), and if the bill is in a former owner's name, ask for a duplicate rather than waiting for a mailing.

Two city chapters can follow a property into a sale.

  • At-risk property registry (Chapter 70.2). Lenders register a property within 15 days of starting foreclosure. Owners of a derelict vacant house register within 30 days. Residential registration is $200, renewed every six months, with a late charge of 10 percent of the semi-annual fee per 30-day period. A buyer takes over the duty and must register or update the file within 15 days of the transfer.
  • Short-term rentals (Chapter 51.5). A yearly license is $25 per unit, and an 8 percent tax applies to gross rental receipts, with monthly returns due by the 20th.

A registered vacant house costs money every six months it stays empty, which makes a prompt as-is sale attractive. Ask the city's building department about open permits or violations before you set a price.

Gather these papers first. Then judge each bid by the amount left in your hands once every payoff is made.

  1. Pull your parcel number and the latest bill from the Treasurer.
  2. Request your recorded deed and make sure the names match the signers.
  3. Check that no city registration charge or code fine is outstanding.
  4. Round up leases and renter contact information if anyone lives there.
  5. Obtain written payoff letters from each lender or lienholder.

Whichever route you pick, closing ends with a title search, a signed deed, the state declaration and county recording. A cash buyer may skip the appraisal, but clean title is still required.

A cash closing can move much faster than a financed one when title is clean, since a financed sale a financed sale waits on the lender's appraisal and underwriting. Ask whoever buys to name the title company, who covers its fee and whether the buyer will take over any leases.

Central Illinois has cold winters and hot, humid summers, so inspectors pay close attention to roofs, heating systems and damp basements. Before you accept an offer, walk through the house the way an inspector would and note what you would flag. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs or credits after the inspection, while a cash buyer generally prices those items into the first offer and moves on. Either way, ask for the number in writing and for the closing date the buyer will commit to.

faqs.q: Will a buyer take a Decatur house with open code problems?
faqs.a: Often yes. Investors regularly buy houses with violations and fix them. Learn from the city what is open so your price reflects it, and settle any registration balance first.

faqs.q: Who covers Illinois transfer tax on a Decatur sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value, and your contract decides which side pays. Confirm with your closing agent, and ask the Recorder if a county stamp also applies.

faqs.q: What are the due dates for Macon County tax bills?
faqs.a: Mailing happens in May, the first installment is due 30 days later, and the second is due September 1 or the next working day. Late payments add 1.5 percent monthly.

faqs.q: Is a license required for a Decatur Airbnb?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 51.5 requires a yearly license for each short-term unit at $25, plus an 8 percent tax on rental receipts filed monthly with the city's Finance Department.

faqs.q: I inherited a Decatur house with unpaid taxes. Where do I start?
faqs.a: Call the Macon County Treasurer at (217) 424-1426 with the parcel number to learn the balance. If the taxes were sold, redemption runs through the County Clerk and includes penalty, costs and interest.
